entries.title: Exodus 16:1
segments: Fifteenth day of the second month; just one month after they started from Egypt.

entries.title: Exodus 16:3
segments:
Kill--with hunger; they had hitherto lived on provisions which they brought with them, or obtained by the way; but as they now entered the wilderness, where they thought they could not obtain any, they feared they should perish. 
 
Men are prone to undervalue their mercies and to magnify their trials. By comparing their present with their past condition they become discontented, and thus unfit themselves for duty and dishonor God.

entries.title: Exodus 16:4
segments: Prove them; put them to trial.  For the meaning of this, see

entries.title: Exodus 16:5
segments:
The sixth day; the sixth working day, the day before the Sabbath. The Sabbath is spoken of as an institution already existing and well known. 
 
Such was God's regard for the Sabbath before the establishment of the Jewish ritual, and before the ten commandments had been written on tables of stone, that he wrought a stupendous miracle, that his people might continue to keep it holy.

entries.title: Exodus 16:6
segments: Ye shall know; by the Lord's providing you a miraculous supply of flesh.

entries.title: Exodus 16:7
segments: Set the glory of the Lord; in the miraculous provision of manna.

entries.title: Exodus 16:8
segments: Not against us; Moses and Aaron acted by God's direction.  The murmurings of the Israelites against them, were therefore in reality murmurings against Him who sent them. Compare

. 
 
When men murmur against others for doing what God commands, instead of blaming men only, they are in reality blaming God.

entries.title: Exodus 16:9
segments: Near before the Lord; near to the cloudy pillar, in which he dwelt, and from which he spoke.

entries.title: Exodus 16:12
segments:
I am the Lord your God; of course all their fears in following his guidance were groundless. 
 
The ingratitude and wickedness of men are often the occasion of wonderful manifestations of the patience, kindness, and grace of God.

entries.title: Exodus 16:14
segments: Round thing; rather, scale-like thing.

entries.title: Exodus 16:15
segments: It is manna; which might be translated, What is this?

entries.title: Exodus 16:16
segments: An omer; the tenth part of an ephah;
.  According to a probable computation, the ephah contained one and one-twelfth bushels English; this would make the omer a trifle less than three and one-half quarts.

entries.title: Exodus 16:18
segments:
Mete; measure. 
 
  Gathered much had nothing over--gathered little had no lack.  These words may be understood in two ways: either that when each head of a family measured out to the members what he had gathered, it was miraculously brought about that there was just an omer apiece; or, that when the people measured the manna with an omer, the superabundance of one man went to supply the want of another.  This seems to be the view taken by the apostle Paul,

. 
 
  According to his eating; according to the number of his household. 
 
Were it best, the Lord could furnish his people with the necessaries of life, and even with luxuries, without their labor; and he sometimes does this.  But generally he requires them to make efforts; and in all cases, having food and raiment, he requires them to be therewith content.

entries.title: Exodus 16:19
segments: Let no man leave of it till the morning; not that each one, under all circumstances, was required to eat the whole, but no one was allowed to lay up any of it or the next day, or for future use.  This was designed to teach them to depend on God, from day to day, for their daily bread.

entries.title: Exodus 16:23
segments:
The Lord hath said; God had told this to Moses, Ex16.5|, and Moses now tells it to the people. 
 
  Seethe; boil. 
 
  Remaineth over; above one omer for a man, or above what they would want for the sixth day. 
 
  To be kept; for their supply on the Sabbath.  It was cooked the day before, to prevent unnecessary labor on the Sabbath. 
 
Things should be so arranged on Saturday that all may rest from worldly employments on the Sabbath, and not be prevented by needless cooking, or any other labor, from remembering the day to keep it holy.

entries.title: Exodus 16:27
segments: However clearly it may be shown that God requires men to keep the Sabbath, some will neglect it.  And though he makes known that men cannot in the end be gainers by disobeying him, yet such as have no love to him, and no confidence in him, will violate the day.

entries.title: Exodus 16:28
segments: My laws; especially those which required them to rest from their ordinary employments, and keep the Sabbath-day holy.

entries.title: Exodus 16:29
segments: Go out of his place; for needless, worldly purposes.

entries.title: Exodus 16:31
segments:
Like coriander-seed; in shape and size. 
 
  Wafers; thin cakes.  When cooked it had something of the taste of sweet oil.

entries.title: Exodus 16:33
segments:
Take a pot; this command seems to be mentioned here by way of anticipation, as the tabernacle was not yet made. 
 
  Before the Lord; in the ark of the testimony, the place of his presence.

entries.title: Exodus 16:35
segments: Forty years; the time they spent in the wilderness.

All which will in the end benefit believers, they will, in the use of suitable means, receive. 
 
"All needful grace will God bestow, And crown that grace with glory too; He gives us all things, and withholds No real good from upright souls."

entries.title: Exodus 16:36
segments: Ephah; see note,
